subject: Terms trade-offs: runtime data scope & subprocessor asks — product/security sync
messages:
From: Maria Lozano <maria.lozano@helixtx.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helixtx.com
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helix DPA redline — two critical asks for runtime exports/subprocessors

Sean — thanks for taking this. Attaching the Helix DPA redline (see Helix_DPA_redline_20270526.docx). Our legal and engineering leads flagged two items we need clarified before we can proceed: 

1) Runtime telemetry / export carveout: We need explicit language that runtime telemetry exported to partners/analytics vendors will be limited to non-identifying metadata (no full payloads or KV cache snapshots), and retention capped at 30 days.
2) Subprocessor list & KMS: We need to know which subprocessors will touch inference payloads and confirmation we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for any export pipeline.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the 30-day retention ask and provide a current subprocessor allowlist + KMS integration note? We are aiming to sign by next week (target 2027-06-03). If you need to escalate to product/security we can wait for that, but please let us know timing.

Thanks,
Maria Lozano
Senior Procurement Manager, Helix Therapeutics
attachments: Helix_DPA_redline_20270526.docx

Subject: Fwd: Helix DPA redline — two critical asks for runtime exports/subprocessors

Team — forwarding Helix's redline. TL;DR: applicant requests 30-day retention on runtime telemetry, restriction of telemetry to non-identifying metadata only, and ability to use customer-managed KMS for any export pipeline. They need answers before 2027-06-03. I attached our internal commentary PDF (SG_internal_commentary_20270526.pdf) with quick notes.

Proposed next steps: 
- Product (Evelyn): confirm feasibility / what is an engineering effort vs config change. In particular, can we reasonably provide a 30-day retention window for runtime KV/cache-derived artifacts?
- Security (Olga): can you confirm the KMS integration constraints and whether the subprocessor allowlist (current list + attestation) is shareable? Also advise on contract language we should offer as counter.
- Sales Ops (Ben): if product/security need time, recommend an interim commitment language or can we offer a limited rollout clause?

CC'ing Maria so Helix sees we're engaging internal owners. If helpful I can set a 30-min sync with product+security today.

—Sean

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helix DPA redline — two critical asks for runtime exports/subprocessors

Thanks Sean — quick product read: 
1) 30-day retention for runtime telemetry / KV-derived artifacts is non-trivial. Our runtime retains some ephemeral KV cache traces tied to recent sessions; those are optimized for serving and for safety debugging. Engineering can implement a pruning policy, but it's a medium-priority effort (estimate: 6–8 weeks to ship a safe, configurable prune-by-age that preserves hot-cache behavior).

2) As a compromise we can offer: 
  - Immediate: limit exported telemetry to a minimal schema (request/response metadata + performance counters) and add a filter to redact PII fields before export. This is a configuration change and can be done in ~1 week.
  - Medium term: targeted KV-cache pruning for Helix (30-day retention) behind a feature flag and an engineering work order.

3) If Helix requires absolute deletion of any "derived artifacts" within 30 days, we need to be explicit about what "derived artifacts" includes — e.g., feature extraction, embeddings snapshots, intermediate logs. Please ask their legal to enumerate examples so we can scope exactly.

I'll put an engineering estimate together today if you want a written timeline for contract redline negotiation. For now I recommend offering the immediate config change + a roadmap commitment to the 30-day prune (with a clear delivery SLA).

—Evelyn Hart
VP Product, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Maria Lozano <maria.lozano@helixtx.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helix DPA redline — two critical asks for runtime exports/subprocessors

Maria / Sean — thanks for the patience. Security/legal review notes and conditional acceptance language below. High level: we can meet Helix's objectives with a few contract conditions and operational commitments.

Required contract changes (suggested language bullets):
- Subprocessor disclosure & attestation: Redwood will provide a current allowlist of subprocessors that may process inference payloads. Redwood will provide written attestation from each subprocessor confirming they will not use customer data for model training.
- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys for exports to external storage. Contract must reference the KMS integration appendix and responsibilities for key rotation and access control.
- Export scope: limit exported telemetry to the agreed minimal schema (non-identifying metadata). Any export pipeline must apply a PII-redaction step prior to storage.
- Retention & remediation: Redwood will commit to a 90-day default for operational logs; for Helix, Redwood agrees to a roadmap commitment to implement a 30-day prune for specified artifact classes within an agreed engineering SLA (I recommend "within 60 days of effective date" for a conservative baseline). If Helix requires a hard 30-day deletion clause with monetary remedies, that requires executive/legal escalation.

Operational evidence to attach before signing: current SOC 2 Type II report, subprocessor attestations, and a diagram of the export pipeline. I can provide SOC2 and subprocessor attestations this week.

Next steps: 
1) Sean — propose we send Helix the conditional counter-redline with the language above and offer the immediate config lock-down (minimal export schema + PII redaction) as an interim control.
2) Evelyn — please confirm you can ship the config change in ~1 week and provide the engineering estimate for the 30-day prune so we can attach a delivery commitment.
3) Ben — coordinate commercial language for the roadmap commitment (e.g., sandboxed feature-flagged delivery window) and any credit/penalty framing if timeline slips.

If all agree, I will produce a short DPA amendment draft and upload to DocuSign; otherwise we'll need to get Legal counsel involved for more formal exceptions.

Olga Petrov
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
attachments: SOC2_TypeII_link (will share), suggested_counter_language.txt
